children: said Tuesday it agreed to acquire a 30% minority interest in Ligga S.A., which operates the Ferro Sul iron ore mine in northern Brazil, after the country’s stock exchange questioned why the deal had not been disclosed to investors.

said the deal includes ~$190M and an exclusive long-term offtake arrangement giving it the right to purchase 100% of Ligga's sinter feed production, securing long-term access to additional volumes of high-quality iron ore.
The transaction is intended to support an expansion plan that would quadruple Ligga's production to 8M metric tons/year from ~2M tons currently, with operations expected to start in June 2028.
The company said production will be transported along the Carajás railroad ~10 km away from the site to the Ponta da Madeira maritime terminal in Maranhão state.
already produces ~330M metric tons/year of iron ore from its two Brazilian operations.

title: Vale to buy 30% stake in Brazil’s Ligga iron ore mine in $190M deal
